MINUTES OF AN ADJOURNED  MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VE RN E
  Tuesday, August 25, 2025

1.  In order to minimize the spread of the COVID 19 Virus, Governor Newsom issued an Executive Order that
  temporarily suspends requirements of the Brown Act. The Council Chambers was closed to the public, La Verne

  City Council Members attended  this meeting telephonically,  and the meeting was live streamed on the City' s
  website.

2.  An adjourned meeting of the La Verne  City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 6: 0  pm.

3.  Council Members  present:  Mayor Tim Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Robin Carder
  Council Member Muir Davis
  Council Member Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory personnel present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress
  Assistant to the City Manager JR Ranells

4.  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Hepburn.

5.  Study Session to Receive a  City Manager Russi reported that the study session was to receive a report
  Report Regarding the Delivery  regarding the delivery of the Fire and EMS
  services.  He stated that Messina &
  of the  Fire and EMS Services  Associates would present the City Council with their findings on the evaluation
  of the County' s Fire Feasibility study for providing fire service as well as a
  review of the City' s existing Fire and Emergency Medical Service operations
  and strategies  for improvement.  No action will be taken regarding the Fire and
  EMS services  by the Council at this meeting. The report will be available and
  public comments will be received for 30 days.

  Tyler Johnson, Messina & Associates gave  a power point presentation.  He
  reported on the high level review of the current Fire and EMS delivery model of
  the La Verne Fire Department and information regarding contracting with Los
  Angeles Fire District for Fire/ EMS service delivery.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter and waited for staff to
  check for any public comment via telephone communication.

  One phone communication from Jim Murphy.

  Public Comment received via email shared with the City Councif is attached.

  After Council  comments  and  their concerns, it was  moved by Carder,
  seconded  by Lau, and unanimously carried to appoint Council Members Davis
  and Crosby to the Fire Feasibility Study Sub- Committee to meet with La Verne
  Firefighters'  Association,  and it was the consensus of the City Council to direct
  the City Manager to contact the County of Los Angeles to explore other
  options not covered in the Fire Study and to look into the City of La Habra
  Fire/ EMS delivery services Model.
   City Council Minutes, Adjourned Meeting, Tuesday, August 25, 2020, Page 2
